items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to surety bond requirements for car dealers
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5485

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to surety
bond requirements for car dealers

PURPOSE:

This bill will increase the required surety bond level for all used
car dealers, with a lower bond level for those with a low volume of
sales, and a higher bond level for those with a high volume of sales.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends paragraph a of subdivision 6-b of section 415 of the
vehicle and traffic law, as amended by chapter 7 of the laws of 2000,
paragraph a as further amended by section 104 of part A of chapter 62
of the law of 2011 to provide that: (1) used motor vehicle dealers
must obtain and maintain a surety bond of $20,000 if they sell fewer
than 50 cars annually, Or a surety bond of $100,000 if they sell more
than 50 cars annually. Dealers who are already bonded must comply with
these provisions by January 1, 2016. (2) Explicitly provides that
surety bonds shall apply to all claims arising from business, acts
and/or omissions by the dealership relating to the sale of motor.
vehicles.  (3) Surety bond issuers must provide notice to the
Department of Motor Vehicles when a dealer's bond lapses. Requires
that the Department of Motor Vehicles verify within five days of a
dealership's bond lapse that the dealership has an active surety bond.

Section 2: This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day
after it shall have become a law.

EXISTING LAW:

Under current law, the surety bond required for new, franchised
dealerships is fifty thousand dollars. Used dealerships who have sold
less than two hundred vehicles in the previous calendar year must
obtain a surety bond in the amount of ten thousand dollars. Used
dealerships who have sold more than two hundred vehicles in the
previous calendar year must obtain a surety bond in the amount of
twenty five thousand dollars.

Currently, no mechanism exists to verify that auto dealers are
maintaining a surety bond after initial issuance.

JUSTIFICATION:

Surety bond levels in New York are inadequate to protect consumers in
the event of a default by dealerships. Currently, most used car
dealerships are only required to obtain a $10,000, or at most, a
$25,000 surety bond. While new, franchised car dealerships are more
heavily regulated within their industry by their associated
manufacturers, used car dealerships have more leeway to operate
independently on their own terms. This creates a higher risk of
deceptive, fraudulent, or otherwise illegal behavior in the industry,
and much of this activity is surfacing in the used car industry.


Ensuring adequate bond levels guarantees that consumers can recover in
the event that they are wronged by a dishonest dealership or lender.

Further, no mechanism exists to verify that dealerships are continuing
their surety bonds, and this allows bad actors to operate without any
surety bond at all, leaving consumers completely vulnerable and unable
to recover any damages.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.
